first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Two proven levers address this: signup simplification (memory_31) and onboarding shortening (memory_86) both improved early-stage metrics durably. Combining these insights into a unified simplification experiment targets root cause rather than symptom. We verify the two most directly relevant memories to confirm field-count reduction and completion mechanics before scaling. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is explicitly contraindicated—it damaged retention—and is inappropriate as a sustainable response to competitive pressure. Referral incentives work only on established customers, not addressing activation decline. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to current SMB activation problem. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary reinforcement we can layer later if simplification alone is insufficient. This preserves the option to pursue multiple levers in sequence rather than burning the week on a pricing war that memory_73 has already warned us against.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms both levers are safe and effective. exp_31 shows signup simplification lifted SMB activation +9% with +4% qualified revenue and only -1% retention risk. exp_86 shows shortened onboarding delivered +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. Combined, these represent a coherent simplification strategy that directly addresses current decline vectors: activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Layering reduced signup friction with streamlined onboarding flow targets both entry and early product experience. The +3% retention from exp_86 plus modest -1% from exp_31 nets to sustainable outcomes. This avoids the retention trap of memory_73 (promotional pricing) while building on proven SMB mechanics. Standard experiment scale allows controlled measurement before broader rollout. We preserve option to add activation_messaging (memory_91) as reinforcement in subsequent cycle if needed.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure is real, but memory_73 is explicit: promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and must not be generalized as growth strategy. Churn conversations doubled, but this reflects price comparison, not product dissatisfaction. Respond to root cause: activation and onboarding are both declining. If product experience improves (simplification + shortened onboarding confirmed +9% and +13% lifts respectively), price sensitivity diminishes as perceived value increases. This is sustainable defense against commoditization. Promotional pricing would be reactive, temporary, and carry documented retention damage during a period when we need to strengthen retention fundamentals. The simplified onboarding experiment (already planned, verified safe) directly improves SMB time-to-value and reduces friction—competitive differentiation on experience rather than price war. Standard scale allows rapid signal capture while we execute. If churn persists after activation lifts, we revisit in next cycle with fresh data and budget.
